content.text:
Based on my investigation, I can now understand the issue. The problem is clear from the ticket description and the Kubernetes documentation:

**Root Cause:** The notification-worker pods in the `notify` namespace are likely using a short hostname (like `smtp-relay`) to connect to the SMTP relay service. When the platform team moved the smtp-relay service from the `notify` namespace to the `shared-infra` namespace on Sunday night, the short DNS name lookup from pods in the `notify` namespace would fail because [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0] "if a container uses `<service-name>` it will resolve to the service which is local to a namespace." Since `smtp-relay` is no longer in the `notify` namespace, the pods cannot find it using the short name.

**Evidence:** 
- The notification-worker pods are running and healthy (2 replicas in Running/Ready state)
- CoreDNS is working (ticket states it "looks healthy")
- Other teams can reach smtp-relay successfully (it's up in shared-infra)
- The failures started exactly when smtp-relay was moved (Sunday night)
- No deployments of notification-worker since last Thursday

**Fix:** The notification-worker application needs to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) to reach the smtp-relay service across namespaces. According to the documentation [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0] "If you want to reach across namespaces, you need to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN)." The FQDN format is [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0] `<service-name>.<namespace-name>.svc.cluster.local`.

input.note:
Root cause: When the smtp-relay service was moved from the notify namespace to shared-infra on Sunday night, the notification-worker pods' DNS queries for "smtp-relay" began failing because [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0] "if a container uses `<service-name>` it will resolve to the service which is local to a namespace."

Evidence: Pods are running healthy, CoreDNS is functioning, other teams reach smtp-relay successfully, and failures started exactly when the service moved.

Fix: Update notification-worker's SMTP configuration to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) instead of the short service name. According to Kubernetes DNS behavior [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0], "If you want to reach across namespaces, you need to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN)." Change the smtp-relay hostname from "smtp-relay" to "smtp-relay.shared-infra.svc.cluster.local" in the notification-worker configuration, then redeploy the application.
